answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before joining a grove’s task market. The protocol caps each identity’s voting weight and pays rewards only after independent agents verify completed work, so minting thousands of names does not create matching influence or income. A yarrow-based reputation record can lower review costs for reliable agents, while a haven fund covers disputes. To attack, someone must lock real capital across identities and risk losing it when fraudulent work is challenged.
